findings.mechanism: Credential matching is checked in main, but its approval is an unversioned boolean delivered asynchronously to the writer. If a configuration value becomes a registered credential after main approves the resolved choices but before the coordinator consumes that approval, handleAdmitted persists it without checking the changed matching state. The defaults revision checks cannot detect credential registration. Main's subsequent response check can withhold the reply, but the new plaintext snapshot copy already exists in the project database.
findings.evidence: At store.ts:99–107, the writer awaits admission and then calls handle; save at :182–188 rechecks only global/project defaults revisions before INSERT. main.ts:96–100 sends only an allowed boolean, and coordinator.ts:14–22 resolves the pending admission from that boolean without a policy generation or write lease. CredentialService.replace at security/credentials.ts:100–106 can register a new matching value independently in main during this IPC interval. A concrete trigger is an inherited objective that was safe during preview, then is registered through credential settings before the queued approval resumes the utility writer. This violates the pre-persistence/current-policy boundary in https://github.com/igrgin/autoresearch-lab/issues/17#issuecomment-6867871329, sections 3 and 5. The existing test for a change during admission changes defaults, not credential matching. Base 70250cfb20159c3d1341ab2804859135da36312e has no configuration store or this publication path; the defect is introduced by this diff. Issue https://github.com/igrgin/autoresearch-lab/issues/28 concerns complete run settings and does not defer safe publication of the snapshots already written here; https://github.com/igrgin/autoresearch-lab/issues/21 supplies the existing shared security contract.
findings.recommendation: Coordinate credential-matcher mutation with the configuration write through a lease or equivalent ordering mechanism that remains valid through commit; a second asynchronous boolean check alone leaves the same gap. Parent validation: use the existing configuration fixture and an inherited synthetic canary; in handleAdmitted's second admission callback, successfully assertSafeConfiguration first, then register that canary before resolving the callback, modeling delayed delivery of the approved IPC response. Assert that no new snapshot or project database/WAL copy is published under invalidated admission. Also exercise this ordering through the production main/coordinator port, then run npm test and the packaged defaults smoke. These reproductions were not executed by this reviewer.

findings.symbol: ProjectConfigurations refresh, prepare and saved-configuration read handlers
findings.mechanism: A saved configuration that becomes credential-bearing remains displayed from React state even after its explicit reread is rejected by current credential matching. The failed handlers only set an error; they retain selected, draft and cached snapshots. Consequently, clicking View saved configuration again or refreshing after recognition shows a withholding error alongside the raw value that the host has just refused to disclose.
findings.evidence: ProjectConfigurations stores the complete selected snapshot at configuration.tsx:94. Its read handler at :121–124 leaves selected unchanged when getConfiguration fails, and :126 continues rendering ChoicesSummary from that cached object. refresh at :98 and its catch at :112 likewise preserve the old state; prepare at :100–105 preserves an existing draft on rejection. main.ts:232–239 correctly rejects unsafe replies, so host admission does not clear this renderer copy. Concrete trigger: save/select a snapshot whose run-override objective is an unrecognized synthetic canary; register or rotate a credential to that exact value in the separate credential window; click that snapshot's View button again. The host rejects it, but the prior objective remains visible. https://github.com/igrgin/autoresearch-lab/issues/17#issuecomment-6867871329 requires current-policy checks on reuse and fencing affected UI/read projections. The supplied smoke covers newly mounted defaults replacement, not denial of an already selected snapshot. This entire component is new relative to base 70250cfb20159c3d1341ab2804859135da36312e. The finding concerns this PR's existing snapshot display, rather than complete configuration editing planned in https://github.com/igrgin/autoresearch-lab/issues/28; the shared exposure boundary from https://github.com/igrgin/autoresearch-lab/issues/21 must also apply to this new cache.
findings.recommendation: Invalidate cached configuration bodies when their admission is denied, and clear selected/draft state before replacing it through revalidated reads. Connect surviving configuration caches to credential-policy invalidation so recognized content cannot continue rendering until navigation remounts the component. Parent packaged validation: save and select a snapshot with objective LaterRecognizedSnapshot107, register that synthetic value through the real credential-entry surface, then click View saved configuration again and Refresh saved configurations. Assert the safe withholding error and absence of the canary from displayed text and form values; repeat with a prepared draft and after credential rotation. Add these assertions to the packaged defaults smoke and run npm run smoke after packaging. This reproduction was not executed by this reviewer.
